title: A quasi-compact scheme has finite specialization-antichain image in a locally Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be quasi-compact (every open covering of $|X|$ has a finite subcover), and let $Y$ be locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $h:X\to Y$ be any morphism. Suppose that for $y,y^{\prime}\in |h|(|X|)$, the inclusion $y^{\prime}\in\overline{\{y\}}$ implies $y=y^{\prime}$, where closure is in the Zariski topology of $Y$. Then the image $|h|(|X|)$ is a finite set. No finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$, and no separation or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $Y$, is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated consequence of Tag 01RL (lemma-quasi-compact-dominant), applied on Noetherian affine target charts to the affine kernel closed image; finite irreducible components: properties.tex Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components). Neither tag alone states this finite-image criterion.

proof.text: Choose an affine open covering $Y=\bigcup_a V_a$, $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$, with every $R_a$ Noetherian, using [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For each $x\in X$ choose $a$ with $h(x)\in V_a$ and, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], an affine open $U_x$ with $x\in U_x\subseteq h^{-1}(V_a)$. These opens cover $X$, so quasi-compactness gives finitely many $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ covering $X$, each with a chosen $V_{a(i)}$. Write $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and $R_i=R_{a(i)}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], the restriction $U_i\to V_{a(i)}$ is induced by its section-ring map $\varphi_i:R_i\to B_i$ and sends a prime $\mathfrak q$ to $\varphi_i^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. It suffices to prove that each such image $E_i$ is finite, since $h(X)=\bigcup_{i=1}^n E_i$.

source.place: Tags 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens), 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine); finite subcover from the stated quasi-compactness hypothesis.

proof.text: Fix $i$, abbreviate $R=R_i$, $B=B_i$, $\varphi=\varphi_i$, and put $K=\ker\varphi$, $A=R/K$, with quotient map $\pi:R\to A$. The map $\psi:A\to B$, $\psi(r+K)=\varphi(r)$, is well defined and injective: equality of the images means $r-r^{\prime}\in K$. For every prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq K$, the subset $\mathfrak p/K=\{r+K:r\in\mathfrak p\}$ is a proper prime ideal of $A$, since products and membership lift along $\pi$, and $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak p/K)=\mathfrak p$. Conversely $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak b)$ is prime containing $K$ for every prime $\mathfrak b$ of $A$, and $\pi(\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak b))=\mathfrak b$ by surjectivity. These inverse operations preserve inclusion, so a prime minimal over $K$ corresponds to a minimal prime of $A$.

source.place: Tag 00FL (lemma-image-dense-generic-points), proof: quotient by the kernel; the elementary prime-ideal correspondence is written out.

proof.text: Let $M$ be the set of prime ideals of $R$ minimal over $K$. This set is finite by [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal], since $R$ is Noetherian. For each $\mathfrak m\in M$, step 2 says $\mathfrak m/K$ is a minimal prime of $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-injective-minimal-prime-lift] to the injective map $\psi:A\to B$. There is a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ with $\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak m/K$. Taking inverse images under $\pi$ gives $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\pi^{-1}(\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q))=\mathfrak m$. Thus every point of $M$ belongs to $E_i$.

source.place: Tag 00FK (lemma-injective-minimal-primes-in-image); Tag 00FR (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), in its arbitrary-ideal form recorded by the cited node.

proof.text: For any $\mathfrak p\in E_i$, contraction shows $K\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] to choose $\mathfrak m\in M$ with $\mathfrak m\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Step 3 places $\mathfrak m$ in $E_i$ as well. In the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\mathfrak p\in\overline{\{\mathfrak m\}}$: every closed set $V(J)$ containing $\mathfrak m$ has $J\subseteq\mathfrak m\subseteq\mathfrak p$, so contains $\mathfrak p$. This specialization in $V_{a(i)}$ is also a specialization in $Y$, because for every closed $F\subseteq Y$ containing $\mathfrak m$, its intersection with $V_{a(i)}$ is closed and contains $\mathfrak p$. Both points lie in $h(X)$, so the hypothesis gives $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$. Consequently $E_i=M$ as subsets of this affine chart, hence $E_i$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), part (4); specialization read directly from the closed sets V(J).

proof.text: The union $h(X)=\bigcup_{i=1}^n E_i$ of these finitely many finite images is finite. If $X$ is empty, take the empty finite subcover and the image is empty. If on a patch $K=R$, then $B$ is the zero ring, so $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $E_i$ are empty; steps 3 and 4 quantify over empty sets and remain valid.

source.place: Finite-union conclusion of the agent argument; zero-ring case from the definition of prime ideal.
